### Install Libraries

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(readxl)
library(xgboost)
library(vip)
library(finetune)
library(doParallel)
```

### Merging Data and Creating Lagged Variables

```{r}
Sub_relation <- read_csv("KnownSubstituteRelationships.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
MBO_data <- read_excel("ManufacturerBackOrderData2025.xlsx")
Weekly_sales <- read_csv(
  "WeeklyMaterialSalesServiceQuantities2025.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(
    .default = col_guess(),
    `DirectOnlyIndicator` = col_character(),
    `RefurbishedItemCode` = col_character()
  )
)
Stock_levels <- read_csv(
  "WeeklyItemStockLevels.csv", 
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(
    .default = col_guess(),
    `RefurbishedItemCode` = col_character()
    )
)

Sub_relation = Sub_relation %>% 
  select(-(...1)) %>% 
  rename(ParentMaterialNumber = "MaterialNumber")

# get just the week calendar (distinct weeks, no duplicates)
week_calendar <- Weekly_sales %>%
  distinct(SalesWeekNumber, WeekStartDate, WeekEndDate) %>%
  mutate(
    WeekStartDate = as.Date(WeekStartDate),
    WeekEndDate = as.Date(WeekEndDate)
  )

MBO_data <- MBO_data %>% mutate(MBOEpisodeStartDate = as.Date(MBOEpisodeStartDate, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))

# join where episode start date falls within the week window
mbo_with_week <- MBO_data %>%
  mutate(MBOEpisodeStartDate = as.Date(MBOEpisodeStartDate)) %>%
  left_join(week_calendar, join_by(
    MBOEpisodeStartDate >= WeekStartDate,
    MBOEpisodeStartDate <= WeekEndDate
  ))

# make mbo_data into a lookup sheet for what products started a backorder in what week
mbo_labeled <- mbo_with_week %>%
  filter(MedlineBrandInd != "Medline Brand") %>%
  distinct(ParentMaterialNumber, SalesWeekNumber) %>%
  mutate(backorder_start = 1)

# create all possible combinations for week and product to ensure that weeks with no activity are accounted
# for so that the model can differentiate between nothing happening in a week and missing data
competitor_mbo_items = mbo_with_week %>% 
  filter(MedlineBrandInd != "Medline Brand") %>% 
  distinct(ParentMaterialNumber)
  
all_weeks = Stock_levels %>% 
  filter(MedlineBrandInd != "Medline Brand") %>% 
  distinct(SalesWeekNumber)

full_panel <- competitor_mbo_items %>%
  cross_join(all_weeks)

# merge panel with mbo lookup sheet and replace weeks with no backorder start with 0s. 
# weeks in a backorder but not the start should be a 0 since we want to predict when the backorders will happen
# and don't need to know their duration

panel_with_target <- full_panel %>%
  left_join(mbo_labeled, by = c("ParentMaterialNumber", "SalesWeekNumber")) %>%
  mutate(backorder_start = replace_na(backorder_start, 0))

table(panel_with_target$backorder_start)

#removing duplicate columns from stock data
join_keys = c("ParentMaterialNumber", "SalesWeekNumber")
Stock_levels_clean = Stock_levels %>% 
  select(-any_of(setdiff(intersect(names(Weekly_sales), names(Stock_levels)), join_keys)))

#final merge
if(file.exists("merged_data.rds")) {
  merged_data <- readRDS("merged_data.rds")
} else {
  merged_data = panel_with_target %>% 
    left_join(Weekly_sales, by = c("ParentMaterialNumber", "SalesWeekNumber")) %>% 
    left_join(Stock_levels_clean, by = c("ParentMaterialNumber", "SalesWeekNumber"))


#remove accidental duplicate rows
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  distinct(ParentMaterialNumber, SalesWeekNumber, .keep_all = TRUE)

# the creation of lag variables
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  arrange(ParentMaterialNumber, SalesWeekNumber) %>%
  group_by(ParentMaterialNumber) %>%
  mutate(
    # --- Fill Rates ---
    fill_rate_lag1 = lag(StockQtyFillRatePerc, 1),
    fill_rate_lag2 = lag(StockQtyFillRatePerc, 2),
    fill_rate_lag3 = lag(StockQtyFillRatePerc, 3),
    fill_rate_drop = fill_rate_lag1 - StockQtyFillRatePerc, # deterioration in fill rate vs last week
    
    service_fill_rate_lag1 = lag(ServiceLineFillRate, 1),
    service_fill_rate_lag2 = lag(ServiceLineFillRate, 2),
    service_fill_rate_lag3 = lag(ServiceLineFillRate, 3),
    
    # --- Backorder Quantity ---
    bo_qty_lag1 = lag(BackOrderQtyEaches, 1),
    bo_qty_lag2 = lag(BackOrderQtyEaches, 2),
    bo_qty_lag3 = lag(BackOrderQtyEaches, 3),
    backorder_rate = BackOrderQtyEaches / (SalesOrderQtyEaches + 1),
    
    eow_bo_qty_lag1 = lag(EndofWeekTotalBackOrderQty, 1),
    eow_bo_qty_lag2 = lag(EndofWeekTotalBackOrderQty, 2),
    eow_bo_qty_lag3 = lag(EndofWeekTotalBackOrderQty, 3),
    
    # --- Stock Levels ---
    unrestricted_stock_lag1 = lag(EndofWeekUnrestrictedStock, 1),
    unrestricted_stock_lag2 = lag(EndofWeekUnrestrictedStock, 2),
    unrestricted_stock_lag3 = lag(EndofWeekUnrestrictedStock, 3),
    stock_drop = unrestricted_stock_lag1 - EndofWeekUnrestrictedStock,
    
    inventory_onhand_lag1 = lag(EndofWeekMonthlyInventoryOnHandQty, 1),
    inventory_onhand_lag2 = lag(EndofWeekMonthlyInventoryOnHandQty, 2),
    inventory_onhand_lag3 = lag(EndofWeekMonthlyInventoryOnHandQty, 3),
    
    open_vendor_po_lag1 = lag(EndofWeekOpenVendorPOStock, 1),
    open_vendor_po_lag2 = lag(EndofWeekOpenVendorPOStock, 2),
    open_vendor_po_lag3 = lag(EndofWeekOpenVendorPOStock, 3),
    
    open_sales_order_lag1 = lag(EndofWeekOpenSalesOrderStock, 1),
    open_sales_order_lag2 = lag(EndofWeekOpenSalesOrderStock, 2),
    open_sales_order_lag3 = lag(EndofWeekOpenSalesOrderStock, 3),
    
    confirmed_sales_order_lag1 = lag(EndofWeekConfirmedSalesOrderStock, 1),
    confirmed_sales_order_lag2 = lag(EndofWeekConfirmedSalesOrderStock, 2),
    confirmed_sales_order_lag3 = lag(EndofWeekConfirmedSalesOrderStock, 3),
    
    # --- Supply/demand ratios ---
    supply_demand_ratio  = EndofWeekUnrestrictedStock / (EndofWeekOpenSalesOrderStock + 1),
    demand_supply_ratio  = SalesOrderQtyEaches / (EndofWeekUnrestrictedStock + 1),
    vendor_po_coverage   = EndofWeekOpenVendorPOStock / (EndofWeekOpenSalesOrderStock + 1),
    backorder_pressure   = EndofWeekTotalBackOrderQty / (EndofWeekOpenSalesOrderStock + 1),
    
    # --- Customer Backorder Metrics ---
    customer_bo_perc_lag1 = lag(CustomerBackOrderPerc, 1),
    customer_bo_perc_lag2 = lag(CustomerBackOrderPerc, 2),
    customer_bo_perc_lag3 = lag(CustomerBackOrderPerc, 3),
    
    bo_customer_ct_lag1 = lag(BackorderCustomerCt, 1),
    bo_customer_ct_lag2 = lag(BackorderCustomerCt, 2),
    bo_customer_ct_lag3 = lag(BackorderCustomerCt, 3),
    
    service_bo_customer_ct_lag1 = lag(ServiceLineBOCustomerCt, 1),
    service_bo_customer_ct_lag2 = lag(ServiceLineBOCustomerCt, 2),
    service_bo_customer_ct_lag3 = lag(ServiceLineBOCustomerCt, 3),
    
    # --- Sales volume and demand trends ---
    sales_order_qty_lag1  = lag(SalesOrderQtyEaches, 1),
    sales_order_qty_lag2  = lag(SalesOrderQtyEaches, 2),
    sales_order_qty_lag3  = lag(SalesOrderQtyEaches, 3),
    demand_growth         = SalesOrderQtyEaches - sales_order_qty_lag1,          # absolute week-over-week change
    demand_growth_pct     = demand_growth / (sales_order_qty_lag1 + 1),          # percentage week-over-week change
    demand_4wk_change     = SalesOrderQtyEaches - lag(SalesOrderQtyEaches, 4),   # acceleration over 4 weeks

    # --- Rolling averages (3-week window smooths out noise for more stable trend signals) ---
    roll_demand_3   = slider::slide_dbl(SalesOrderQtyEaches,  mean, .before = 2, .complete = FALSE),
    roll_backorder_3 = slider::slide_dbl(BackOrderQtyEaches,  mean, .before = 2, .complete = FALSE),
    roll_fill_3     = slider::slide_dbl(StockQtyFillRatePerc, mean, .before = 2, .complete = FALSE),
    
    # --- Seasonality ---
    week_of_year = SalesWeekNumber %% 52  # captures recurring seasonal demand patterns
) %>% 
    ungroup()

# --- Substitute demand features ---
# aggregate weekly sales for each substitute product
sub_demand <- Weekly_sales %>%
  group_by(SubstituteMaterialNumber = ParentMaterialNumber, SalesWeekNumber) %>%
  summarise(
    sub_sales = sum(SalesOrderQtyEaches, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
)

# join substitute relationships to their weekly sales
subs_features <- Sub_relation %>%
  left_join(sub_demand, by = "SubstituteMaterialNumber", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  group_by(ParentMaterialNumber, SalesWeekNumber) %>%
  summarise(
    total_sub_demand = sum(sub_sales, na.rm = TRUE), # total demand across all substitutes
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# join substitute features onto main panel
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  left_join(subs_features, by = c("ParentMaterialNumber", "SalesWeekNumber"))

merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  mutate(
    sub_demand_ratio = total_sub_demand / (SalesOrderQtyEaches + 1)
  )

# replacing NAs that should be 0s because there is no known substitute
merged_data = merged_data %>% 
  mutate(
    total_sub_demand = replace_na(total_sub_demand, 0),
    sub_demand_ratio = replace_na(sub_demand_ratio, 0)
  )

# removing NAs
merged_data = merged_data %>% 
  select(-c("RefurbishedItemCode", "DirectOnlyIndicator")) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(demand_growth)) ## dropping rows where lagged variables are NA

saveRDS(merged_data, "merged_data.rds")
}
table(merged_data$backorder_start)

### worth noting that removing NA lagged variables removed about 1300 rows where 
### backorders started in the first 4 weeks of the year. ratio is still consistent with pre-drop ratio,
### but worth noting.
```

```{r}
#| include: false 
rm(Stock_levels, Weekly_sales, Sub_relation, MBO_data,
   panel_with_target, xgb_grid, cv_folds)
gc()
```

### Building Machine Learning Model

```{r}
# time for the fun stuff (ML model)
# make backorder_start a factor instead of numeric 
merged_data_model = merged_data %>% 
  mutate(backorder_start = as.factor(backorder_start))

# split data into test and training sets (ordered by time)
if(file.exists("train.rds") & file.exists("test.rds")) {
  train = readRDS("train.rds")
  test = readRDS("test.rds")
} else {
  split_week = quantile(merged_data_model$SalesWeekNumber, .8) # first 4 quantiles are training sets
  train = merged_data_model %>% filter(SalesWeekNumber <= split_week)
  test = merged_data_model %>% filter(SalesWeekNumber > split_week)
  saveRDS(train, "train.rds")
  saveRDS(test,"test.rds")
}

# print out number of rows in test/train sets and make sure backorder rates are similar in each set
cat("Train rows:", nrow(train), "\n")
cat("Test rows:", nrow(test), "\n")
cat("Train backorder rate:", mean(train$backorder_start == "1"), "\n")
cat("Test backorder rate:", mean(test$backorder_start == "1"), "\n") # checks out!

# recipe (preprocessing instructions to apply before data is actually fed into model)
rec <- recipe(backorder_start ~ ., data = train) %>% #predicts backorder start based on all other variables
  update_role(ParentMaterialNumber, WeekStartDate, WeekEndDate, MedlineBrandInd, SalesWeekNumber,
              new_role = "ID") %>% # makes sure these
    #vars aren't used for prediction, only reference
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) %>% # handles new levels in test/validation
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) %>% # handles NAs before dummying
  step_other(all_nominal_predictors(), threshold = 0.01) %>%  # collapses rare categories
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>% # converts categorical variables into dummy vars
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>% # removes columns where every row is the same value; prevents inclusion
    #of columns with no predictive info which would cause model errors
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) #replaces any remaining numeric NAs to be that column's median

# define model and parameters
xgb_spec = boost_tree(
  trees = 500,
  tree_depth = tune(),
  learn_rate = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune(),
  sample_size = tune()
) %>% 
  set_engine ("xgboost", scale_pos_weight = 47) %>% # weight backorder starts 47x heavier
    #than weeks without a backorder start. 47 comes from our number of 0s divided by our number of 1s.
    #without weighting, the model would be incentivized to predict 0 for everything and get a 97.9%
    #success rate
  set_mode("classification") # we are predicting whether a backorder starts in a given week or not,
    #so this is a classification problem

xgb_workflow = workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(rec) %>% 
  add_model(xgb_spec)
```

### Cross Validation

```{r}
# time for tuning
if(file.exists("cv_folds.rds")) {
  cv_folds = readRDS("cv_folds.rds")
} else {
  cv_folds = sliding_window( # sliding window allows each fold to train on past weeks 
    #and validate parameters on future weeks; future data is never available and overfitting
    #on patterns the model wouldn't have access to is prevented. k-folds cv would allow model
    # to peek at future data resulting in an artificially better prediction model
    train,
    lookback = round(nrow(train) * 0.6), # train on 60% of rows
    assess_stop = round(nrow(train) * 0.1), # evaluate on the next 10%
    step = round(nrow(train) * 0.05) # slide forward 5% each fold
  )
  saveRDS(cv_folds, "cv_folds.rds")
}

cat("Number of CV folds:", nrow(cv_folds), "\n") # 6: great number of cv folds to have!
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# prepare for massive CPU load
parallel::detectCores()
registerDoParallel(cores = parallel::detectCores() - 1)
```

```{r}
# set tuning parameters
set.seed(11)
xgb_grid = grid_random( 
  tree_depth(range = c(3, 10)),
  learn_rate(range = c(-3, -1), trans = log10_trans()),
  min_n(range = c(2, 100)),
  loss_reduction(range = c(-5, 0),   # added - controls tree splitting threshold
                 trans = log10_trans()),
  sample_size = sample_prop(range = c(0.5,1)), # added - row subsampling
  size = 50
)

if(file.exists("xgb_tuned.rds")) {
  xgb_tuned = readRDS("xgb_tuned.rds")
} else {
  xgb_tuned = tune_grid(
    xgb_workflow,
    resamples = cv_folds,
    grid      = xgb_grid,
    metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, f_meas, precision, recall), # definitions: roc_auc - ability
     #to discriminate backorder vs non-backorder week. precision - TP / (TP + FP). recall -
     #TP / (TP+FN). f_meas - harmonic mean of precision and recall. note: claude believes that
     #recall matters more as it costs Medline more to miss a real shortage (FN) than to occasionally
     #have a FP
    control   = control_grid(verbose = TRUE, parallel_over = "everything")
  )
  saveRDS(xgb_tuned, "xgb_tuned.rds")
}
```

```{r}
#| include: false 
rm(Stock_levels, Weekly_sales, Sub_relation, MBO_data,
   panel_with_target, xgb_grid, cv_folds)
gc()
```

```{r}
# plot AUC to determine how good the parameters are
show_best(xgb_tuned, metric = "roc_auc")
autoplot(xgb_tuned)

# select best params based on roc_auc
best_params = select_best(xgb_tuned, metric = "roc_auc")

# finalize workflow with best params
final_workflow = xgb_workflow %>% 
  finalize_workflow(best_params)

# fit on full training set and evaluate on test set
if(file.exists("final_fit.rds")) {
  final_fit <- readRDS("final_fit.rds")
} else {
  final_fit <- final_workflow %>%
    last_fit(split = initial_time_split(merged_data_model, prop = 0.8))
  saveRDS(final_fit, "final_fit.rds")
}

# evaluate on test set
collect_metrics(final_fit)

### results key ###
# accuracy doesn't buy us much here because of class imbalance. the model
# could predict 0 every time and get 97.9% accuracy. #

# ROC AUC indicates the probability that between a random backorder-start
# week and a random non-backorder-start week, the backorder-start week has a
# higher predicted probability. this is important for Medline as it is better
# to falsely predict that there will be a shortage than to predict no shortage
# because it is more costly to miss a real shortage. #

# Brier Score measures the accuracy of probability predictions where 0 
# is perfect. #
```

### Evaluation Metrics, Setting Threshold, Plots

```{r}
# confusion matrix
collect_predictions(final_fit) %>% 
  conf_mat(truth = backorder_start, estimate = .pred_class)

# precision (positive pred. value) recall (true positive rate) curve
collect_predictions(final_fit) %>% 
  pr_curve(truth = backorder_start, .pred_1) %>% 
  autoplot()

# distribution of predicted probabilities
collect_predictions(final_fit) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = .pred_1)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of predicted backorder probabilities")

# ROC curve
collect_predictions(final_fit) %>% 
  roc_curve(truth = backorder_start, .pred_1) %>% 
  autoplot()

### default threshold of 0.5 is far too high and the model is not 
### flagging shortage starts. we need to lower the threshold to be
### where predicted probabilities are: between 0 and 0.02. ###

# find threshold that maximizes f1 score (harmonic mean of
# precision and recall)
# this is important as Medline wants to balance catching
# real shortages against raising false alarms
pr_data = collect_predictions(final_fit) %>%
  pr_curve(truth = backorder_start, .pred_1)

# summarize tradeoff across candidate thresholds
threshold_summary <- tibble(threshold = c(0.003, 0.0035, 0.004, 0.005, 0.006, 0.007)) %>%
  mutate(
    results = map(threshold, ~collect_predictions(final_fit) %>%
                    mutate(pred = as.factor(ifelse(.pred_1 >= .x, 1, 0))) %>%
                    summarise(
                      caught    = sum(pred == 1 & backorder_start == 1),
                      missed    = sum(pred == 0 & backorder_start == 1),
                      false_alarms = sum(pred == 1 & backorder_start == 0),
                      precision = caught / (caught + false_alarms),
                      recall    = caught / (caught + missed)
                    ))
  ) %>%
  unnest(results)

threshold_summary

### we'll go with a threshold of 0.0035. with this threshold, the model will
### identify 59% of competitor shortages 1-3 weeks before they occur. in
### this case, Medline would review about 7100 weekly alerts to find 705 real
### shortage event. we believe 0.0035 to be the best threshold because it balances
### number of false alarms and percentage of real shortages. ###

# apply chosen threshold
optimal_threshold <- 0.0035

final_predictions <- collect_predictions(final_fit) %>%
  mutate(
    .pred_class_adjusted = as.factor(ifelse(.pred_1 >= optimal_threshold, 1, 0))
  )

conf_mat(final_predictions, truth = backorder_start, estimate = .pred_class_adjusted)

# --- feature importance ---
final_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  vip::vip(num_features = 15) +
  labs(title = "Top 15 Most Important Features for Predicting Competitor Backorders")
```
